root_idea.summary: The root centers on losing, missing, or departing from the proper course, whether literally, intellectually, morally, or in the outcome of an action.
root_idea.development: From loss of a way or object, the meanings extend to error and straying, disappearance or concealment, perishing and annulment, and causatively to leading another into error.

senses.definition: To go astray, deviate from what is right, or miss the proper way.
senses.usage_conditions: Used both intransitively and with a way or course understood; the Qur'an applies it to error, deviation, and loss of right direction.

senses.definition: To become lost, perish, or come to nothing.
senses.usage_conditions: Includes the loss or annulment of an undertaking and, in the Qur'anic expression concerning the body, becoming dust and bones.

senses.definition: To be absent from awareness or memory; to forget or be unmindful.
senses.usage_conditions: In Qur'anic constructions this includes a lapse of memory and the statement that nothing escapes or is forgotten by the Lord.

senses.definition: To cause someone to go astray, mislead, or turn away from right guidance.
senses.usage_conditions: The causative may describe human or satanic misleading and divine letting or causing someone to remain in straying; the latter is presented in the Qur'anic discussion as connected with the person's prior course or disposition.

senses.definition: To cause something to perish, be lost, or become without effect.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of works, plots, and other outcomes that are rendered futile, unrecognized, or unrecompensed, as well as of causing a person or thing to be lost.

senses.definition: More astray, farther from the right course, or most astray.
senses.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative evaluation of distance from right guidance; the degree of straying varies with the comparison and context.

senses.definition: One who is straying, deviating from right guidance, or lost.
senses.usage_conditions: The active participle can function adjectivally or substantivally and may describe a continuing state or its result.

senses.definition: Not yet guided or unaware of the guidance sought; in some contexts, forgetful or in a state of inadvertence.
senses.usage_conditions: This Qur'anic use need not imply culpable doctrinal error; it includes a temporary or situational lack of awareness and the state described in the account of Moses.

senses.definition: Straying, error, or deviation from the right course.
senses.usage_conditions: May concern intellectual beliefs, religious practice, moral judgment, or any departure from the approved way; it may be intentional or inadvertent and slight or extreme.

senses.definition: Perdition, loss, or the annulled state of a thing or action.
senses.usage_conditions: Used when something is lost, perishes, or fails to produce its intended result; this includes the Qur'anic description of a state of perdition.

senses.definition: A state or instance of straying, error, or deviation from the right course.
senses.usage_conditions: The noun is semantically equivalent to ضَلَال in the Qur'anic usage and can denote the condition or occurrence of being astray.

senses.definition: One who causes another to go astray; a misleader.
senses.usage_conditions: The Qur'anic form is substantivized for an agent who misleads or leaves another without right guidance.

senses.definition: Leading astray, misleading, or causing deviation from the right way.
senses.usage_conditions: Names the action or process corresponding to Form II ضَلَّلَ.

senses.definition: Rendering an undertaking futile, lost, or annulled.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Qur'anic construction concerning the plot of the أصحاب الفيل, the term denotes an outcome of destruction, futility, or annulment rather than merely verbal misleading.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To miss or lose the location of a stationary thing, such as a road, mosque, house, or animal, without finding the way to it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use applied to something whose place is not found; distinct from merely deviating oneself from a path.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become confused or perplexed and unable to see the right course.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional extension describing disorientation rather than the ordinary fact of going astray.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become unperceived, hidden, concealed, or absent from view.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes a road or object becoming hidden from someone; the memory-related Qur'anic uses are listed under the Quranic form sense for forgetting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go away from someone so that he cannot reach or find the person who departed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A special transitive construction meaning that a person has gone beyond the speaker's ability to compass him.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attribute or impute error or deviation to someone or to an undertaking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a Form II use distinct from actively leading someone into error.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To send cattle out to pasture or set them free to graze where they please.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bury and thereby hide or conceal a person or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical use, including the expression for a dead person being buried.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find someone to be erring, astray, or not rightly directed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical pattern comparable to other Form IV verbs meaning to find someone in a particular state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become beyond someone's power or ability to compass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tropical use describing something that has passed beyond the speaker's reach.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To go away or disappear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the construction describing water disappearing from beneath a stone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To feign being astray, confused, or unable to find the right way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form indicates pretended rather than genuine straying.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have one's straying demand or produce still more straying.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional Form X expression describing error as the occasion of further error.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of being lost, perishing, coming to nothing, or passing away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantival use derived from ضَلَّ and ضَاعَ or هَلَكَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An unknown person, one in whom there is no good, or one who persists in error.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed descriptive expression, also used of a person regarded as worthless or persistently mistaken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vain, futile, or misleading thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantival and idiomatic use in which the thing comes to nothing or misleads without result.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Confusion, perplexity, or error; also going away without knowing where one has gone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can describe an action done in error or a departure whose destination is unknown.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Speech about a person in his absence or behind his back, whether favorable or unfavorable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized conventional use of the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Skill in guiding or directing aright during a journey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun with a meaning opposite in practical effect to ordinary straying.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Unlawful or non-legitimate birth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression for someone being another's son unlawfully begotten or not trueborn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Blood that goes unavenged or without retaliation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed expression describing a killing for which no retaliation is exacted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who has no good in him, including a cunning or harmful person; in one expression, a follower of women.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Conventional idiomatic descriptions rather than the ordinary adjective meaning astray.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person in whom there is no good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical use reported on the authority of Meyd; it is distinct from the ordinary noun senses of confusion, error, or speech in a person's absence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water running beneath a rock or among trees, hidden from the sun.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal description of concealed or sheltered running water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Absence or a state of concealment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A broader Classical nominal sense distinct from the Qur'anic noun's principal sense of error or straying.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who errs or goes astray much or persistently, especially one not directed toward good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive descriptive form, also applied to one who does not desist from error.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stray or lost animal, or any lost thing whose owner or location is unknown.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to male or female animals, to singulars and plurals, and extended to anything lost and sought.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rugged, hard, stony land or ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reduplicated nominal describing difficult terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stone, or stones, small enough to be lifted and carried, especially smooth stones in a valley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized terrain term for movable valley stones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skillful guide of the way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use distinct from the rugged-land sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The remains of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the plural expression for water left behind.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In the fixed expression, to fall into futility, disappointment, or destruction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom may describe entering what is vain and unreal or perishing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road, land, trial, discord, or mirage that causes one to go astray.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A non-personal agentive adjective; the Qur'anic substantivized personal-agent use is listed separately.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause of straying, or a place such as a land or desert in which one loses the way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used both as a substantive for a cause of error and as an epithet for misleading terrain; the vocalized variant مَضِلَّة is cross-referenced to the same branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who pretends to be astray or confused.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle of Form VI, contrasted with someone who is genuinely able to be guided.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Core Form I straying and transitive loss of a stationary object.
Becoming lost, perishing, or coming to nothing.
Death and becoming dust are covered by the Quranic loss/perishing sense.
Memory-related absence is Quranic; generic concealment is Classical.
Going beyond another's ability to find or compass.
Form II causing error and attributing error.
Finding someone in an erring state.
Pointer to the earlier Form I discussion.
Fixed expression for an unknown or worthless person.
Idiomatic loss or perdition, with an alternate futile sense.
Confusion/error and speech in a person's absence.
Attributed specialized sense of a person without good.
Primary nominal sense of deviation and error.
Pointer to ضَلَالٌ; the corresponding Quranic meaning is independently covered.
Quran-attested active participle meaning astray or lost.
Becoming lost is covered by the active-participle sense.
Fixed idiom for futility, disappointment, or perishing.
Road, land, trial, or mirage that causes straying.
One who pretends to be astray.

cautions: The QAC nominal أَضَلُّ is presented as a comparative adjective and is not merged with the Form IV verb أَضَلَّ.
The active participle ضَالّ has a Qur'anic use for a state of not yet being guided or of inadvertence; this should not automatically be equated with culpable doctrinal error.
Lane's historical Quran citation notation was used only as lexical evidence; modern verse locations in examples are taken from independently supplied QAC occurrences.
